content.comment_body: Hello, this is my first post. I need additional inputs and outputs on my [product_name] system. I've acquired another [product_name] base module and would like to know if it's possible to control outputs on the second module by logging in to the first via [product_name] web editor. I saw a demonstration on assigning an input to an output on another module—if I trigger that input using the web editor, will the output on the other module activate?
Hello [user_name], welcome to the forum. Yes, this is possible. For an example, please share which exact [product_name] modules you are using.
Thank you! I'm running a 12/24 [version_no] with three [product_name] digital modules. Two are on the first base module, one on the second. An example would be greatly appreciated.
I need the [article_no]s, which should start with [article_no].
[article_no] and [article_no]
Do you have two [product_name] units with those [article_no]s? If so, I can create an example for you.
Yes, two of those units and three [product_name] digital modules of the other [article_no].
Here is a basic example.
Thank you, I'll try it tomorrow. Is a network hub necessary between the two modules, or can separate cables be used in the same subnet?
A standard network switch will work. The [product_name] modules must be on the same subnet.

I've got everything running, but the network output from the client [product_name] to the slave [product_name] isn't working. Both modules are set to master and slave modes. In simulation, the network output works from the web editor, but the signal doesn't reach the slave module. They're on the same subnet. I'm attaching my project.
On both [product_name] modules, be sure to activate S7 access. Go to File > Properties > Offline settings > General.

Still not working; all flags in simulation respond from the web editor, but Q1 on the second module is still inactive. Inputs I1 and I4 are configured as momentary break—they work in standard simulation, but in the online test, when I activate them from the web editor, the inputs don't show as active (not red). Why does this happen?

I'm unsure about your setup, as your [product_name] program appears different from the one initially uploaded, and your actual web editor project hasn't been posted. I can't determine the issue without seeing your current files. When setting M3 to 1 in simulation, it works as expected.
Here is the web editor project.

Since I have only one [product_name] with [version_no], I changed the slave unit to [version_no]. I then adjusted the IP addresses accordingly, uploaded both the web editor project and [product_name] programs, and confirmed everything works. See attached video.

Now both units are working in master mode—thanks! Another question: I have an indicator for Q1 (switch button) on the first module. Is it possible to display an indicator for Q1 from the second module in the web editor?
You'll need to transfer the variable from module 1 to module 2.
Can you explain how to do that with an example?
Please refer to the attached example.
Thank you, your technical expertise and willingness to help are greatly appreciated.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is seeking advice on expanding their [product_name] setup with additional modules and digital expansion modules. They want guidance on how to control outputs on a secondary device using the web editor and are unsure about network configuration and communication between modules in the same subnet.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to log in to the main [product_name] module and remotely control outputs on a secondary module via the web editor, aiming for seamless operation over the network.
pain_keywords: lack of clear multi-device configuration guidance
